verses.zh: 旷野和干旱之地必然欢喜；沙漠也必快乐；又像玫瑰开花，
verses.en: Let the wilderness and desert be happy;[NOTE:1] let the arid rift valley[NOTE:2] rejoice and bloom like a lily!
notes: The final mem (ם) on the verb יְשֻׂשׂוּם (yesusum) is dittographic (note the initial mem on the following noun מִדְבָּר [midbar]). The ambiguous verbal form is translated as a jussive because it is parallel to the jussive form תָגֵל (tagel). The jussive is used rhetorically here, not as a literal command or prayer.

This verse employs three terms for desolate places: מִדְבָּר (midbar, “wilderness”), צִיָּה (tsiyyah, “dry place, desert”), and עֲרָבָה (ʿaravah, “rift valley”). A midbar is an area that receives less than twelve inches of rain per year. It may have some pasturage (if receiving six to twelve inches of rain), but often has desert-like qualities. A tsiyyah is not a sandy desert per se, but of the three terms most clearly indicates a dry, desert region. The rift valley includes the Jordan Valley, but it still has a reputation as a dry, desolate place from its conditions near the Dead Sea and southward.
verses.commentary:
35:1 "wilderness" This word refers to the uninhabited pasture land of southern Judah (BDB 184, cf. Joel 1:19-20).

▣ "the desert" This word (BDB 851) refers to the arid, sterile land (cf. Isa. 41:18; 53:2;
Joel 2:20). Notice that "wilderness" is linked to "desert" and parallel with "Arabah."

▣ "Arabah" This word (BDB 787) refers to the Jordan rift valley south of the Dead Sea
(cf. Isa. 33:9).

▣ "will rejoice and blossom" The first two VERBS of Isa. 35:1
are also a parallel personification of the plants.

- will be glad, BDB 965, KB 1314, Qal IMPERFECT
(possibly JUSSIVE in meaning), this VERB
is used eight times in chapters 61-66

- will rejoice, BDB 162, KB 189, Qal JUSSIVE, cf. Isa. 35:2; 25:9;
this VERB is used four times in chapters 61-66, cf. Joel 2:21,23

The third VERB "blossom," "bud" (BDB 827, KB 965, Qal
IMPERFECT with INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE of the same root,
which shows intensity) shows how the plants (i.e. personified) rejoice. Isaiah often uses
personification of natural items (cf. Isa. 33:9; 44:23; 55:12, cf. NASB Study Bible, p. 1004). The
conditions of the Garden of Eden (Genesis 1-2) are restored; the new age has come!

Verse 10 is repeated in Isa. 51:11. This is a sign of the new age of restoration (cf.
Isa. 7:21-25; 27:6; 32:15; 41:8-19; 55:12-13).

SPECIAL TOPIC: EDEN

SPECIAL TOPIC: MESSIANIC ERA

verses.zh: 必开花繁盛，乐上加乐，而且欢呼。黎巴嫩的荣耀，并迦密与沙仑的华美，必赐给它。人必看见耶和华的荣耀，我们　神的华美。
verses.en: Let it richly bloom;[NOTE:1] let it rejoice and shout with delight![NOTE:2] It is given the grandeur[NOTE:3] of Lebanon,the splendor of Carmel and Sharon.They will see the grandeur of the Lord,the splendor of our God.
notes: The ambiguous verb form תִּפְרַח (tifrakh) is translated as a jussive because it is parallel to the jussive form תָגֵל (tagel).
Heb “and let it rejoice, yes [with] rejoicing and shouting.” גִּילַת (gilat) may be an archaic feminine nominal form (see GKC 421 §130.b).
Or “glory” (KJV, NIV, NRSV); also a second time later in this verse.
verses.commentary:
35:2 "Lebanon. . .Carmel and Sharon" These three areas were famous for their lush foliage. The phrase
"blossom profusely" is the Qal INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE and Qal
IMPERFECT VERB of the same root (BDB 827, KB 965) which denotes intensity or
here, lush growth.

▣ "They will see" This seems to be a continuing of the personification of the plants.

▣ "the glory. . .the majesty" Notice the parallel between

- glory (BDB 458, KB 455; see SPECIAL TOPIC: GLORY[ OT])

- majesty (BDB 214) is used of YHWH as

- Victor ‒ Ps. 45:4-5

- Creator ‒ Ps. 96:6; 104:1; 111:2-3

- Judge ‒ Isa. 2:10

Also notice the parallel between

- YHWH ‒ see SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.

- Eloah ‒ see SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, C.

verses.zh: 你们要使软弱的手坚壮，无力的膝稳固。
verses.en: Strengthen the hands that have gone limp,steady the knees that shake.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “staggering knees”; KJV, ASV, NRSV “feeble knees”; NIV “knees that give way.”
verses.commentary:
35:3-6 These verses mention several kinds of people.

- the exhausted (lit. "weak hands")

- the feeble (lit. "weak knees")

- those with anxious hearts (lit. "the hurried")

- the blind (BDB 734)

- the deaf (BDB 361)

- the lame (BDB 820)

- the dumb (BDB 48)

YHWH uniquely cares for the poor, weak, sick, lonely, and socially ostracized. Here is a list of
what God will do for them in this new day of restoration.

- for #1 "encourage" (BDB 304, KB 302, Piel IMPERATIVE)

- for #2 "strengthen" (BDB 54, KB 65, Piel IMPERATIVE)

- for #3

- take courage, BDB 304, KB 302, Qal IMPERATIVE

- fear not, BDB 431, KB 432, Qal IMPERFECT
but JUSSIVE in meaning

- for #4 "open the eyes," BDB 824, KB 959, Niphal IMPERFECT

- for #5 "open the ears," same VERB as #4

- for #6 "leap like a deer," BDB 194, KB 222, Piel IMPERFECT

- for #7 "tongue of dumb will shout for joy," BDB 943, KB 1247, Qal
IMPERFECT

This is the message that Jesus sent to John the Baptist while he was in prison (cf. Matt. 11:4-5;
Luke 7:20-22). The New Age is reflected in the ministry of Jesus!

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEALING

verses.zh: 对胆怯的人说：你们要刚强，不要惧怕。看哪，你们的　神必来报仇，必来施行极大的报应；他必来拯救你们。
verses.en: Tell those who panic,[NOTE:1] “Be strong! Do not fear!Look, your God comes to avenge;with divine retribution he comes to deliver you.”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “Say to the hasty of heart,” i.e., those whose hearts beat quickly from fear.
The jussive form וְיֹשַׁעֲכֶם (veyoshaʿakhem), which is subordinated to the preceding imperfect with vav conjunctive, indicates purpose.
verses.commentary:
35:4 Notice what YHWH promises to do for His covenant people.

- He comes with vengeance, BDB 668, cf. Isa. 34:8; 59:17; 61:2; 63:4; Deut. 32:25; Jer. 50:28

- His recompense also comes, BDB 168, cf. Isa. 59:18 (twice); 66:6, also note 65:6

- He will save them, BDB 446, KB 448, Hiphil JUSSIVE, cf. Isa. 25:9;
33:22; 38:20; 45:17; 49:25; 59:1; 63:1,5,9; 64:5

SPECIAL TOPIC: SALVATION (OT)

verses.zh: 那时，瞎子的眼必睁开；聋子的耳必开通。
verses.en: Then blind eyes will open,deaf ears will hear.

verses.zh: 那时，瘸子必跳跃像鹿；哑巴的舌头必能歌唱。在旷野必有水发出；在沙漠必有河涌流。
verses.en: Then the lame will leap like a deer,the mute tongue will shout for joy;for water will burst forth in the wilderness,streams in the arid rift valley.[NOTE:1]
notes: The rift valley (עֲרָבָה, ʿaravah) extends from Galilee to the Gulf of Aqaba. Near the Dead Sea and southward its conditions are very dry and desolate. Other translations render it as “desert” (KJV, NIV, NRSV), “wastelands” (NLT), or by its Hebrew name, “the Arabah” (NASB).
verses.commentary:
35:6 "For waters will break forth in the wilderness" The blooming of nature goes back to Isa. 35:1,2. The
outward sign of God's spiritual presence and blessing is nature's wonderful display of beauty and growth
(cf. Isa. 35:7). This was the blessing for covenant obedience from Lev. 26 and Deut. 28. See full note at Isa. 32:20.

SPECIAL TOPIC: WATERS

verses.zh: 发光的沙（或译：蜃楼）要变为水池；干渴之地要变为泉源。在野狗躺卧之处，必有青草、芦苇，和蒲草。
verses.en: The dry soil will become a pool of water,the parched ground springs of water.Where jackals once lived and sprawled out,grass, reeds, and papyrus will grow.
verses.commentary:
35:7 "In the haunt of jackals" The Peshitta and KJV translate this word (BDB 1072) "dragons." We have
found from the Dead Sea Scrolls that animals listed in the OT often refer to the idols of the surrounding
nations, therefore, this either refers to

- a deserted place

- the residence of the demonic (cf. Isa. 34:11-15)

The literary reason for this poetic line is that the dry dens of the jackals are now filled
with water and can support swamp grass.

NASB
"its resting place"

NKJV
"where each lay"

NRSV
"a swamp"

NJB, REB
"their lairs"

Peshitta
"habitation"

The MT has רבצה, BDB 918,
"her resting place." The NRSV changes it to לבצה,
"swamp, BDB 130 (see NIDOTTE, vol. 1, p. 692-693). The DSS scroll of Isaiah has "he lies down."
The UBS Text Project, p. 81, gives the MT a "C" rating (considerable doubt). The jackal's den is
now flooded.

▣ "Grass becomes reeds and rushes" The grass will grow as tall as reeds and rushes to show
the luxurious growth of God's blessing symbolized in nature (i.e. plenty of water everywhere).

verses.zh: 在那里必有一条大道，称为圣路。污秽人不得经过，必专为赎民行走；行路的人虽愚昧，也不致失迷。
verses.en: A thoroughfare will be there—it will be called the Way of Holiness.[NOTE:1] The unclean will not travel on it;it is reserved for those authorized to use it[NOTE:2]—fools[NOTE:3] will not stray into it.
notes: The Hebrew text reads literally, “and there will be there a road and a way, and the Way of Holiness it will be called.” וְדֶרֶךְ (vederekh, “and a/the way”) is accidentally duplicated; the Qumran scroll 1QIsaa does not reflect the repetition of the phrase.

The precise meaning of this line is uncertain. The text reads literally “and it is for them, the one who walks [on the] way.” In this context those authorized to use the Way of Holiness would be morally upright people who are the recipients of God’s deliverance, in contrast to the morally impure and foolish who are excluded from the new covenant community.
In this context “fools” are those who are morally corrupt, not those with limited intellectual capacity.
verses.commentary:
35:8 "the Highway of Holiness" This is a common theme in the book of Isaiah (cf. Isa. 26:7; 40:3-4; 42:13).
This same imagery of a royal visit is used to describe the coming of the Messiah. John the Baptist claims
he fulfilled the prophecy of Mal. 4:5 in preparing the way for the Lord. This is imagery for preparation
of a physical road, but it has spiritual implications referring to repentance.

▣ Line 3 and line 5 speak of the same person being excluded from returning. YHWH will
accompany His faithful people, therefore, any "unclean" person must be excluded. In this context, "fools" equal
"the unclean."

This divinely created highway of holiness is for those who have repented and believed (cf. v. 10).

▣ "fools" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: FOOLISH PEOPLE

verses.zh: 在那里必没有狮子，猛兽也不登这路；在那里都遇不见，只有赎民在那里行走。
verses.en: No lions will be there,no ferocious wild animals will be on it[NOTE:1]—they will not be found there.Those delivered from bondage will travel on it,
notes: Heb “will go up on it”; TEV “will pass that way.”
verses.commentary:
35:9 "No lion will be there" The fact that vicious animals will be absent or changed into tame
companions is a sign of a blessing of God (cf. Isa. 11:6-9). It is also a reversal of the threat
of Lev. 26:22.

SPECIAL TOPIC: LIONS IN THE OT

▣ "the redeemed" This term was first used in connection with the dedication of the firstborn
child to God (cf. Exod. 13:13,15). The primary idea here is of deliverance from bondage at a set price. The
relationship between "redeemed" (BDB 145 I, KB 169, Qal PASSIVE PARTICIPLE)
in Isa. 35:9 and "ransomed" (BDB 804, KB 911, Qal PASSIVE PARTICIPLE)
in Isa. 35:10 is repeated in Isa. 51:11.

SPECIAL TOPIC: RANSON/REDEEM

verses.zh: 并且耶和华救赎的民必归回，歌唱来到锡安；永乐必归到他们的头上；他们必得着欢喜快乐，忧愁叹息尽都逃避。
verses.en: those whom the Lord has ransomed will return that way.[NOTE:1] They will enter Zion with a happy shout.Unending joy will crown them,[NOTE:2] happiness and joy will overwhelm[NOTE:3] them;grief and suffering will disappear.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “and the redeemed will walk, the ransomed of the Lord will return.”

Heb “[will be] on their head[s].” “Joy” may be likened here to a crown (cf. 2 Sam 1:10). The statement may also be an ironic twist on the idiom “earth/dust on the head” (cf. 2 Sam 1:2; 13:19; 15:32; Job 2:12), referring to a mourning practice.
Heb “will overtake” (NIV); NLT “they will be overcome with.”
Heb “grief and groaning will flee”; KJV “sorrow and sighing shall flee away.”
verses.commentary:
35:10 "the ransomed of the Lord" See SPECIAL TOPIC: RANSOM/REDEEM.

▣ "will return" This VERB (BDB 996, KB 1427, Qal
IMPERFECT) means "turn back" (i.e. repentance or change of direction). Many
commentators see this (and Isa. 35:8) as a reference to the return from Babylonian exile (i.e. therefore
is connected to chapters 40-66). This is surely possible because Isaiah's poems are not always arranged
in chronological order. It could express "repentance" as a lifestyle (i.e. a Highway of Holiness, v. 8).

SPECIAL TOPIC: REPENTANCE (OT)

▣ "Zion" This later came to be a designation for the entire city of Jerusalem (built on seven hills),
in particular the temple, although the temple is geographically located on Mt. Moriah, not on Mt. Zion.

SPECIAL TOPIC: ZION

▣ The returnees are characterized as

- the ransomed of the Lord

- coming with singing

- coming with everlasting joy

- having on their heads as a crown

- joy

- gladness

- having no sorrow

- having no sighing

▣ The NET Bible, p. 1242, #16, has an interesting comment.

"'Joy' may be likened here to a crown (cf. 2 Sam. 1:10). The statement may also be an ironic
twist on the idiom 'earth/dust on the head' (cf. 2 Sam. 1:2; 13:19; 15:32; Job 2:12), referring
to a mourning practice."

SPECIAL TOPIC: GRIEVING RITES

▣ "With everlasting joy upon their heads" The term "everlasting" is 'olam (BDB 761).

SPECIAL TOPIC: FOREVER ('olam)

▣ "And sorrow and sighing will flee away" See Isaiah 25:8 and Revelation 21:4.

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which
means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the
light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not
relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare
your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is
the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every
paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- This chapter is obviously the reversal of Isaiah 34.

- The question is to whom it is addressed and when.

- Does this refer to the agricultural splendor of the Promised Land in the eschaton
(i.e. believing faithful Jews and Gentiles)?

- Does this refer to the return of the Assyrian captives to Palestine (i.e. Israel)?

- Does this refer to the return of the Babylonian exiles by Cyrus' decree (i.e. Judah; Jer. 31:7-9)?

- Does this refer to the desert between Mesopotamia and Palestine being transformed
into a lush highway for God's people to return to Palestine (i.e. the fastest way for returnees
to come back to Palestine)?

- Remember, Isaiah is an anthology of his sermons, but

- the historical setting is not specified

- the sermons are not in chronological order

- the method of arrangement seems to be word sound plays as a way of linking sermons together

- these poems were delivered orally with someone besides the prophet himself writing them down

- This historical ambiguity allows Isaiah's predictions to apply to both the Assyrian and Neo-Babylonian exiles,
as well as Cyrus II allowing refugees to return to Judah.

This is where the theological concept of "inspiration" must be expanded to include later editors or
compilers. Moderns do not know when or how the OT as we know it was complied or arranged.
